patronage: Europe, converts from Judaism, martyrs of the Holocaust

en.name: Edith Stein
en.summary: German-Jewish philosopher who converted to Catholicism and became a Carmelite nun, murdered at Auschwitz for her Jewish ancestry.
en.body: Edith Stein was a brilliant German philosopher, a student and assistant of Edmund Husserl and one of the first women in Germany to earn a doctorate in philosophy, raised in an observant Jewish family before a long intellectual and spiritual journey led her to Catholicism, reportedly triggered in part by reading the autobiography of Teresa of Avila in a single overnight sitting. She entered the Carmelite order, taking the name Teresa Benedicta of the Cross, and continued writing influential philosophical and theological work even as Nazi racial laws increasingly targeted anyone of Jewish descent regardless of religious conversion. Transferred to a convent in the Netherlands for safety, she and her sister Rosa, also a convert, were arrested in 1942 in reprisal for a Dutch bishops' public condemnation of Nazi deportations, and both were deported to Auschwitz, where Edith was murdered in the gas chambers. She was canonized by Pope John Paul II in 1998 and declared a co-patroness of Europe, honored both as a martyr of the Holocaust and as a significant modern philosopher.
